title: Gig: hang a launch banner off Skybridge Tower's mezzanine. The boss offers C$150 to skip the harness check.

options.label: Do the check anyway
options.cost: The C$150 bonus, and his sighs

outcomes.text: You check the harness. One strap is frayed. The boss sighs, swaps it and doesn't mention the bonus again.

later.text: Remember checking the harness at Skybridge Tower? The building's safety manager heard. She asked for you by name on a better gig.

outcomes.text: No check, no problem. The banner says 'DISRUPT EVERYTHING' and you get C$150 for not disrupting your schedule.
A strap gives. You slide six feet into a decorative ficus. You're fine. The ficus is not. You still get the C$150.

options.label: Skip it, ask for C$300
options.riskWhy: Bosses talk on the gigs board

outcomes.text: 'C$300 or I check every buckle twice.' He pays. You skip it. The banner goes up. So does your price.

later.text: Remember shaking down the Skybridge banner boss for C$300? He pinned a note on the gigs board: 'Will skip safety, for a fee.'

title: Gig: build a pop-up stage for a startup launch. Skip the weight test, finish early, C$120 bonus.

options.label: Test it properly
options.get: A stage that holds a CEO

outcomes.text: You stack sandbags and jump on it. One leg wobbles. You fix it. Valentina watches, writes something down, says nothing.

options.label: Skip it, take the C$120
options.cost: Peace of mind during the speech
options.riskWhy: A wobbly leg and a big founder

outcomes.text: You skip the test and leave by six. The stage holds. The founder's speech about 'moving fast' is very on theme.
You skip the test and take the C$120. The founder steps up. The stage creaks. It holds. Barely.

later.text: Remember skipping the stage test? It tilted during the founder's 'we never cut corners' line. The clip is everywhere. So is your name.

options.label: Test the front, skip the back
options.get: C$60 and a mostly safe stage
options.cost: Half the work, half the worry

outcomes.text: You test where the founder stands and trust the rest. The boss pays half the bonus for half the corner cut.

title: On the gigs board: C$200 to post five-star reviews of The Tipsy Turnstile, a bar you've never been to.

outcomes.text: You pass. The gig is gone in four minutes, to someone whose profile says 'review enthusiast.'

options.label: Post the five stars
options.cost: Your word, for a bar you've never seen

outcomes.text: 'Life-changing negronis. Bartender has kind eyes.' You've never been there. C$200 lands in four seconds.

later.text: Remember the five stars for The Tipsy Turnstile? The review site wiped all 40 of them and pinned a 'paid reviewer' label on your profile.

options.label: Go, then post an honest one
options.cost: An evening there, and the owner's mood
options.riskWhy: He paid for five stars, not three

outcomes.text: You go. The negronis are fine. The bartender has normal eyes. You post three honest stars and keep the C$200.

later.text: Remember your three honest stars for The Tipsy Turnstile? The owner demanded his C$200 back. He settled for C$100 and a long sulk.

title: Moving gig on 21st Street: the client hands YOU the C$120 tip. Kenji carried the couch up alone.

outcomes.text: You hand Kenji sixty. He nods like you passed a test you didn't know you were taking.
'You carried the couch.' Kenji stares at the money, then at you. 'Nobody does that.' You did that.

later.text: Remember giving Kenji the whole tip on 21st Street? He passed you a moving gig of his own: a piano, a pro crew and C$150.

outcomes.text: C$120 in your pocket. Kenji asks if the client tipped. You say 'she said thanks.' That's also true.

later.text: Remember the tip on 21st Street? The client's review thanked 'both movers for the C$120.' Kenji read it. So did Valentina.

title: Your gig client never checks hours. You worked six. The form says 'Hours: ___.'

outcomes.text: '6.' Valentina's app approves it in a second. It is the only app in Queens that works.

later.text: Remember writing six honest hours? Valentina's app flagged you as 'reliable' and pushed you a pro gig first.

outcomes.text: '8.' Rounded up for vibes. Approved. Nobody blinks.
'8.' Approved. For now.

later.text: Remember writing eight hours for six? Valentina's audit matched the door log. She took the C$80 back with a very polite note.

options.label: Write twelve
options.riskWhy: Twelve hours on a six-hour job?

outcomes.text: '12.' You stare at the number. It stares back. Approved, somehow.

later.text: Remember the twelve-hour invoice for a six-hour gig? Valentina took it back and benched you from pro gigs for the week.

title: Valentina trusts you to house-sit a client's penthouse in Long Island City. The roof deck fits sixty.

options.label: Water the plants, go home
options.get: C$150 and a client for life

outcomes.text: You water fourteen plants, feed one very judgmental fish and leave. C$150. The fish approves.

later.text: Remember house-sitting the LIC penthouse like a saint? The client booked you for a whole month of weekends. C$200 up front.

options.label: Invite one friend for the view
options.riskWhy: One guest, one glass, one wipe

outcomes.text: One friend, one bottle of seltzer, the whole skyline. You wipe every glass twice. Nobody will ever know.
Sixty people, a DJ named Polaroid, and the best roof photos of your life. The fish has seen things.

later.text: Remember the 'small' party at the LIC penthouse? The doorman's log said 61 guests. The client found a sequin in the fish tank. Valentina dropped you.

title: A Skybridge client leaves you her keys, her cat and a fridge full of C$90 cheese while she's in Lisbon.

options.label: Feed the cat, touch nothing
options.cost: The cheese, which is calling you

outcomes.text: You feed the cat, scoop the box and stare at the cheese like a museum piece. C$120, and your dignity.

later.text: Remember not touching the Lisbon client's cheese? She came home, counted it (she counts it), and sent you a wedge plus a C$50 tip.

options.label: Just a nibble of each
options.get: C$120 and the best snack of your life

outcomes.text: A sliver of each, smoothed over with a butter knife. The aged gouda alone was worth a week's mood.

later.text: Remember 'just a nibble' of the Lisbon client's cheese? She counts her cheese. Her review: 'Cat great. Cheese suspicious.'

outcomes.text: She replies from Lisbon: 'Take the brie, it turns Friday.' You eat the brie with a clear conscience.
She replies: 'Please don't.' You don't. The cat eats its food. You eat a Steinway Fresh yogurt.
